summary: The root أجج (Ajj) primarily describes the act of kindling or setting something ablaze, causing it to burn fiercely.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.

headwords.def: أَجَّتِ النَّارُ , (S, A, Msb,) aor. اَجُجَ (S, Msb) and اَجِجَ , (M, TA,) [the former contr. to analogy, and the latter agreeable therewith, in the case of an intrans. verb of this class,] inf. n. أَجِيحٌ , (S, A, Msb, K,) The fire burned, burned up, burned brightly, or fiercely, (Msb,) blazed, or flamed, or blazed or flamed fiercely; (S, A, Msb, K;) as also (S, A, K) and [written with the disjunctive alif اِيتَجَّت ]: (S, K:) or made a sound by its blazing or flaming. headwords.gloss: He made the fire to; burn, burn up, burn brightly; fiercely
headwords.def: أجّج النَّارَ , (S, A, K,) inf. n. تَأْجِيحٌ , (K,) He made the fire to [ burn, burn up, burn brightly or fiercely, (see 1,)] blaze, or flame, or blaze or flame fiercely. (S, A, K.) [Hence,] أجّج بَيْنَهُمْ شَرَّا (assumed tropical:) He kindled evil, or mischief, among them. (TA.)

headwords.gloss: It gave light; shone; shone brightly

parts.t: (TA, from a trad.) See also 8, where a contracted form of this verb is mentioned.

headwords.def: تَاَجَّجَ see 1. Hence تإجّج also signifies It gave light; shone; or shone brightly. (TA, from a trad.) See also 8, where a contracted form of this verb is mentioned.

headwords.gloss: The day was; became, intensely hot; fiercely burning
headwords.def: إِاْتَجَجَ see 1. [Hence,] ائتجّ النَّهَارُ [written with the disjunctive alif اِيْتَجَّ ] The day was, or became, intensely hot, or fiercely burning; (S, K;) as also and تأجّج . (K.)

headwords.gloss: Intenseness of heat; its fierce burning; The intense heat

parts.t: of an ostrich running, and of people walking or passing along. (A.) You say,
The people are in a state of confusion

headwords.def: أَجَّةٌ Intenseness of heat, and its fierce burning; (S, K;) as also [inf. n. of 1], and , and [inf. N. of 8]: pl. إِجَاجٌ . (S.) You say, جَآتْ أَجَّةٌ الصَّيْفِ The intense heat, or fierce burning, of summer came. (TA.) The sound of fire; as also . (ISd, TA.) (tropical:) The sound, or noise, and commotion, of an ostrich running, and of people walking or passing along. (A.) You say, أَجَّ أَجَّةَ الظَلِيمِ [explained above: see 1]. (A.) (assumed tropical:) Confusion: (S, K:) or, as also , the confusion arising from the talking of a people, and the sound, or noise, of their walking or passing along. (L.) You say, القَوْمُ فِي أَجَّةٍ The people are in a state of confusion [&c.]. (S.)
